messages:
kevin: Heads-up — hitting a starvation pattern in continuous-batching when the queue-proxy process restarts. small tenants get pinned behind large long-running batches. repro + logs below, cc @anya @marta

anya: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro? is this the same oddity from last week's canary? :thinking:

kevin: minimal steps: 1) start 5 tenants, one tenant emits 1k concurrent short requests, others emit 5-10 reqs/sec. 2) restart queue-proxy on the node handling the 1k tenant. 3) after restart, the big tenant immediately floods backlog and due to our proxy admission it holds the slot tokens until its stream drains -> small tenants wait.

kevin: logs snippet: ```
I0321 11:02:13 queue-proxy.go:212 Accept(tenant=big-tenant, tokens=512)
I0321 11:02:13 admission.go:87 LeaseAcquire(tenant=big-tenant, headroom=1024) -> GRANTED
I0321 11:02:15 queue-proxy.go:345 ProxyRestarted -> rehydrates leases, but missing ephemeral windows
I0321 11:02:16 scheduler.go:401 Admit -> small-tenant blocked waiting on slot (owner=big-tenant)
```

marta: we saw something similar but we handled it w/ preemptive eviction. That has cost implications — evicting inflight batches loses tokens and may increase tail lat. Two rough approaches: 1) make proxy restart rehydrate soft-windows + decay timers so new arrivals can preempt long holders; 2) change admission to keep a tiny reserved fastpath for small tenants (burst queue).

li: worth enumerating invariants: - no tenant should be able to permanently block others - we must not degrade latency for high-throughput tenants drastically - operations must be simple to reason about for canary rollouts. Also: add metrics to expose "queue.proxy.window_rehydrate_missing" and per-tenant "hold_time_ms".

kevin: agreed on metrics. current proxy persists leases to etcd but we only persist coarse credits, not transient accept-windows. on restart transient windows collapse. two-option sketch: 
* A: persist ephemeral window token count with TTL, so restart picks up soft windows. pros: minimal changes; cons: heavier etcd churn, TTL races.
* B: change runtime logic so that proxy restart sets a small global admission override: for next Xs allow up-to N short requests per tenant irrespective of lease. pros: simple & local; cons: another global knob and possible fairness leak.

anya: what about hybrid: persist just a single-bit marker per-tenant "recently-active" + last_active_ts; on restart if last_active_ts < threshold treat tenant as cold and move them to low-priority queue. that avoids persisting heavy counters but gives us a fallback for restarts.

marta: hybrid seems attractive. but corner-case: big tenant doing many tiny requests will look "recently-active" and still starve others. can we combine hybrid + micro-reservations? e.g., per-tenant burst-credit = min(persisted_credits, global_burst_cap).

li: metrics + simulation needed. I can add queue-proxy sim harness to run these mixes (persisted tokens vs hybrid) and measure per-tenant p99 and fairness (e.g., Jain index) under restarts. estimate ~1d to wire sim + dashboards.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary cluster has 4 nodes available for queue-proxy testing. Use tag `qp-rehydrate-canary` for safe rollout.

kevin: proposed immediate short-term plan: (1) add metrics (window_rehydrate_missing, per-tenant hold_time_ms) + small sim harness (li) (2) implement hybrid marker (anya) + config knob `proxy.rehydrate_strategy=hybrid` (3) run canary under `qp-rehydrate-canary` with synthetic workload. if sim looks good, iterate on micro-reservations.

anya: I'll take hybrid marker impl. will aim for a PR by EOD tomorrow. I'll make marker TTL configurable.

marta: i'll draft a short RFC blurb describing tradeoffs (persist counters vs hybrid vs global override) so we have a record for later refactor.

li: starting sim work now. will push a dashboard with fairness curves into #observability by EOD.

kevin: thanks all. after canary we'll check telemetry for "queue.proxy.window_rehydrate_missing" spikes and tenant p99 regressions. if we see >10% small-tenant p99 increase we rollback the canary. :thumbsup:

anya: note for PR: keep default `proxy.rehydrate_strategy=none` so behavior is unchanged until we flip config at canary.

marta: ack. adding `ops: canary` to RFC when i post it.

kevin: closing loop — created ticket INF-1827 to track follow-ups (sim results, PR, RFC). I'll update thread with ticket link once created.
